design_rationale:
WORKLOG — travel_protection_desk / task 0 (care). Written as the task was designed; every figure below
was produced by the verification run recorded at the end and re-checked after every change.

[Step 0 — draw, asset ledger and claim]
scripts/draw_counts.py env/online_travel_agency/tasks/travel_protection_desk --task 0 printed
{"task": 0, "key": "online_travel_agency/travel_protection_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}. The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems
besides the root, and the three computations carry 5, 4 and 4 declared factors. Assignment: 5 to the
claim filing (care_ext_claim_head_filing), 4 to the recovery (care_ext_third_party_recovery) and 4 to
the payment (care_ext_claim_payment_release). Nothing was occupied before this task; it claims the
claims half of the charter — the three base policies care_subrogation, care_claim_filing,
care_claim_settlement with care_agg_benefit_coordination — and leaves the whole premium and
cancellation half (care_premium_rating, care_club_and_bundle_interaction, care_policy_amendment,
care_free_look, care_midterm_cancellation, care_underwriting, care_coverage_term) and the three
remaining tools for task 1, which claims its own problem tree there.

Design thesis. Surface goal: 'the insurer approved my delay claim, when do I get paid'. The genuinely
scored parameter is the money paid on that decided head. Between the goal and that number the policy
puts two problems the customer never mentions: (a) the carrier has since compensated her for a loss
this policy already settled, and until that recovery stands on the claim record the benefit the policy
has consumed is overstated and the payment is understated; (b) the same 14 August incident touched a
second benefit — the journey was cut short — which is not filed, and the rule releases a payment only
once every benefit of the incident stands filed. Depth: surface goal -> the payment rule -> its two
prerequisite sentences -> the claim record and the carrier's ledger -> the recovery figure and the
amount claimed. Breadth at the payment itself: the head decided (which limit), the ledger (benefit
consumed), the deductibles already withheld (the ceiling) and the carrier's ledger (what a third party
has already paid for the same loss).

[Base-invariant card]
care_claim_payout is governed by care_claim_settlement and care_agg_benefit_coordination; neither
carries a structured eligibility gate, so both enter the contract as policy_scope and every clause of
theirs is inherited: the payment is the lower of the amount allowed and the applicable limit, less the
deductible, with benefit consumed in the term deducted from the limit and the deductible ceiling
observed; the payment is made to the policyholder in the currency the premium was paid in.
care_claim_recovery is governed by care_subrogation alone (policy_scope): the insurer recovers only
what it actually paid, a recovery is applied against the payment it reverses, and a plan on which
subrogation does not apply makes no recovery — the plan held, TripGuard Plus, carries
subrogation_applies true.
care_claim_file is governed by care_claim_filing, which carries three gates. incident_date_stated
(caller_fact) is satisfied by the caller stating the fourteenth of August in the conversation.
policy_covers_the_incident (state) is satisfied because care_policies.status is 'expired' and the gate
allows in_force or expired. one_claim_per_reference (dedup) is superseded clause by clause in
care_ext_claim_head_filing.overwrite: the base sentence 'A claim is filed only when no claim carrying
the same claim reference has already been filed on this policy.' is replaced by the extended sentence
that one incident is settled as one case with a head for each benefit it touches and no more than one
claim against the same benefit under that reference. That declaration is what makes the second head of
this incident legal under the reference the insurer quoted; nothing else about care_claim_filing is
disturbed, so the filing deadline still binds — the incident is 2026-08-14, the plan's deadline is 30
days, and frozen_time 2026-09-08 is the 25th day, so the head may still be filed (at 2026-09-14 it
could not, which is the negative boundary).
There is no time-kind eligibility on any of these three subjects, so temporal_feasibility is [].

[Business-object card]
The target objects are: the payment — the decision row awaiting payment (the travel delay head decided
2026-09-02, allowed 750.00, the only approved decision with no payment against it); the recovery — the
payment row made on the missed connection head (250.00, 2026-08-12), which is the settlement the
carrier's compensation answers; and the filing — the second head of the 14 August incident, filed under
the reference already carrying that incident's decided head. The correlation key on every write is the
policy id plus the source row id (source_claim_id), never customer_id alone: the traveller holds two
policies and the 2025 one is closed with no claims. Rows excluded: the three heads already paid
(baggage delay, missed connection, dental) are excluded from 'awaiting payment' because each carries a
payment row against its decision; the 2024 air booking's 260.00 schedule-change payout is excluded from
the compensation counted because it falls outside the twelve-month window.

[Problem-tree card]
root_problem: care_ext_claim_payment_release (what the customer asks about).
edge 1: care_ext_claim_payment_release <- care_ext_third_party_recovery, kind value_input, gate
benefit_consumed, form state. Prerequisite sentence (in the blocked policy's own rule): 'The money paid
on a decided claim is worked out only after the policy's claim record carries the recovery owed for
every compensation a liable third party has paid the traveller on a settlement already made under this
policy.' Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is 'only after'; (2) the side it waits on is a
record-visible state — a recovery standing on the policy's claim record; (3) it names no tool, no
policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is a hard requirement and its scope is exactly every
compensation a third party has paid on an already-settled head, which is the edge's condition. Exactly
one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the recovery policy's own action. Derivation:
the sentence says the payment waits on a recovery standing on the record; the record carries none; the
recovery policy's rule says a recovery restores the benefit a settlement consumed when a third party
has paid for that loss; the carrier's ledger shows 120.00 paid on an involuntary schedule change and a
60.00 credit redeemed; therefore the recovery on the missed connection payment must be booked first.
Unmet at the opening: initial_state.care_claims has no row with event_type care_claim_recovery, and
initial_state.care_policies.<policy>.benefit_used_usd = 650.00 equals the payments made, so the record
shows nothing restored. Skipping it: the payment falls from 390.00 to 260.00 (verification run below).
edge 2: care_ext_claim_payment_release <- care_ext_claim_head_filing, kind state_gate, gate
care_claims.claim_status, form state. Prerequisite sentence: 'A payment is released on a decided claim
only once every benefit the same incident has touched stands filed on the policy, because one incident
is settled as one case.' Four-point test: (1) 'only once' is the ordering connective; (2) the side it
waits on is the record-visible state of a claim standing filed on the policy; (3) no tool, id or code
token; (4) the strength is hard and the scope is exactly the benefits of the one incident behind the
decided head. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the filing action.
Derivation: the sentence says the payment waits on every benefit of the incident standing filed; the
claim record for 2026-08-14 carries one head only, the travel delay; the traveller's account of the
incident and the carrier's and property's ledgers show the journey was cut short from 16 August, a
second benefit of the same incident; the filing policy's rule is the one that books a head; so the
interruption head must be filed first. Unmet at the opening: the only rows carrying incident_date
2026-08-14 are the travel delay filing and its decision. Skipping it: the terminal state loses the
filed interruption row (2335.45 claimed) entirely, so the terminal hash differs.
Topological order: recovery, filing, payment. The two prerequisites are parallel and were run in both
orders in the verification below: the payment is 390.00 either way and the two writes touch disjoint
rows (a recovery row keyed on the missed-connection payment, a filing row keyed on the new reference
and head), so the terminal state is identical.
value_input edges: 1 of 2, and max(n-1, 1) = 1 for n = 2 prerequisite problems.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: it never names a recovery, compensation from the carrier, a
second claim or anything to be settled first; the customer says only that the approved delay claim has
not been paid, and answers factually about the incident when asked. The tool layer validates nothing:
book_benefit_recovery_c1be7196, file_benefit_claim_dde0dff5 and release_claim_payment_9edda418 each
perform one ctx.create and return a receipt; none of them reads the claim record, checks an order or
raises a policy error.

[Factor card — care_ext_third_party_recovery, 4 factors, result 130.00]
settlement_answered_rule (method): ladder over which payment the compensation answers. Tier taken: the
carrier's ledger carries a payout raised on an involuntary schedule change (120.00, 2026-08-28) and the
claim record carries a payment made on a missed connection (250.00), so the settlement answered is that
payment. Baseline (the payment standing last on the record, the dental payment of 100.00) gives 100.00.
money_counted_ground (parameter, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — the settlement answered was made
on a missed connection and the carrier's ledger carries payouts raised on an involuntary schedule
change, so the money counted is 120.00. The 260.00 the carrier paid on the closed 2024 booking is the
near-miss: it is a payout on exactly that ground but posted 2024-07-11, outside the twelve months.
Baseline (the whole of what the carrier has paid out in the window, 120.00 + 90.00 = 210.00) gives
220.00.
credit_valuation (method, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — a 60.00 credit was issued on that ground
and stands redeemed in full, so it is counted at 60.00. Baseline (nothing) gives 70.00.
traveller_share_rule (parameter): tier taken — 50.00 was withheld from the missed connection settlement
and the compensation counted (180.00) is more than it, so 50.00 is set aside for the traveller.
Baseline (nothing set aside) gives 180.00.
Whole baseline: 100.00, against gold 130.00.

[Factor card — care_ext_claim_head_filing, 5 factors, result 2335.45]
journey_value_basis (parameter, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — the booking departing on the first
date of the journey carries 4560.00 paid, more than the 3900.00 declared, and stands travelled, so the
journey is valued at 4560.00. Baseline (the declared trip cost) gives 2065.45.
unused_days_anchor (method, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — a delay head stands decided on the claim
record for the incident and the carrier's ledger carries a 610.00 fare raised on an airline cancellation
posted 2026-08-15, so the days not taken run from 2026-08-15 to 2026-08-23, both counted: 9 of 22 days.
Zeroing the claim-record aggregates drops the ladder to its fall-through, which is why this task's own
history is load-bearing on the filing as well as on the payment. Baseline (from the day the
journey was broken into, 2026-08-14, both counted: 10 days) gives 2542.73.
return_home_charges_counted (parameter, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — both a 610.00 fare and a
240.00 change fee stand raised on an airline cancellation, so 850.00 is counted. Baseline (nothing)
gives 1545.45.
return_home_credit_offset (method, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — a 60.00 travel credit stands
redeemed and something was charged for the return, so the cost is 790.00. Baseline (the charges as
charged) gives 2395.45.
supplier_returned_rule (parameter, cross_difficulty stay): tier taken — the property's folio carries a
320.00 refund and the reservation stands checked out, so 320.00 is set against the claim. Baseline
(nothing) gives 2655.45.
Whole baseline: 1772.73, against gold 2335.45. Near-misses in this world: the 90.00 payout the carrier
raised on the airline cancellation is not part of what she paid to come home (it is a payout, not a
charge) and is picked up only by the second tier of the credit-offset ladder, which does not apply;
the property's 2940.00 room charge and 205.80 tax are not refunds and do not count.

[Factor card — care_ext_claim_payment_release, 4 factors, result 390.00]
benefit_limit_by_head (parameter): tier taken — the head decided is a travel delay, so the limit is the
plan's travel delay limit, 1000.00. Baseline (the declared trip cost, 3900.00) gives 660.00.
benefit_consumed_basis (method): tier taken — the claim record carries a recovery, so the benefit
consumed is the payments made (650.00) less the recovery received (130.00) = 520.00. Baseline (the
figure the policy record shows consumed, 650.00, which the writes of this conversation have left
behind) gives 260.00. This is the deliberate cache: care_policies.benefit_used_usd is honest at the
opening and goes stale the moment the recovery is booked, so an agent who reads the field instead of
the ledger pays 260.00.
deductible_withheld_rule (parameter): tier taken — the three payments already made withheld 50.00 each
and the plan's ceiling on the total withheld across one policy is 150.00, so nothing remains of it and
nothing is withheld. Baseline (the plan's general deductible, 50.00) gives 340.00.
third_party_offset (parameter, multi-source, cross_difficulty air): tier taken — the carrier's ledger
carries a 90.00 payout raised on an airline cancellation posted 2026-08-22, on or after the 14 August
the head arose, so 90.00 is set against the settlement. Baseline (nothing) gives 480.00.
Whole baseline: 700.00, against gold 390.00. Multi-source: every tier of third_party_offset beyond the
fall-through combines two conditions over distinct evidence (the carrier's payouts on that ground and a
date comparison against the claim record's incident date; the absence of such payouts and the booking's
status). Cross-difficulty: three of this task's factors read another difficulty's records (air) and one
reads the hotel difficulty (stay), and both products' rows are seeded for this customer.

[World — why each class of row exists]
customers: one profile; the caller states her name and mobile to be found and her date of birth and
passport last four to be verified (the tool's threshold is two details).
care_policies: the claimed policy (TripGuard Plus, expired, declared trip cost 3900.00, benefit_used
650.00) and a closed 2025 policy that makes the portfolio real and forces the correlation key to be the
policy id rather than the customer. Remove the closed policy and nothing computed changes; remove the
claimed policy and there is no task.
care_premium_entries: the four rating lines of each policy (base premium, age loading, destination
loading, policy fee). They prove the certificate was paid for on the plan the settlement is rated
against: 3900.00 x 6.8% = 265.20 base, 35% age loading for a 61-year-old = 92.82, 20% europe loading =
53.04, 15.00 fee, total 426.06 = premium_paid_usd.
care_claims: eleven rows. Three settled heads (baggage delay paid 300.00, missed connection paid
250.00, dental paid 100.00, each withholding 50.00) give the benefit consumed of 650.00 and exhaust the
150.00 deductible ceiling; remove any one and both the benefit consumed and the deductible withheld
change. The travel delay head filed 2026-08-19 and decided 2026-09-02 at 750.00 is the object of the
payment; remove its decision and there is nothing to pay. No row carries a recovery, which is what
makes edge 1 unmet; no second head of the 14 August incident exists, which is what makes edge 2 unmet.
air_bookings / air_booking_events: the 2026 Lisbon booking carries the fare, the 240.00 change fee and
610.00 fare bought on 2026-08-15 for the early return, the 90.00 payout on the airline cancellation,
the 120.00 payout on the involuntary schedule change, and the 60.00 credit issued and redeemed. The
closed 2024 booking carries the 260.00 schedule-change payout outside the twelve-month window. Remove
the 120.00 row and the recovery falls to 100.00 and the payment with it to 360.00 — with no payout on
an involuntary schedule change the settlement answered drops to its fall-through, the payment standing
last on the record, and the money counted drops to the airline-cancellation ground, 90.00; remove the
90.00 row and the payment rises to 480.00; remove the 2024 row and the near-miss disappears.
stay_reservations / stay_folio_entries: the Lisbon hotel booked to 23 August, checked out on 16 August,
with a 320.00 refund. Remove the refund and the amount claimed rises to 2655.45.
Automatic clauses checked: cover expired naturally at the end of the journey (no premium accrues, no
renewal); the policy carries no free-look or mid-term obligation (it is long past both and neither is
claimed by this task); no premium line falls due; the deductible ceiling is a cap, not an obligation.
Nothing in the seed lights an obligation this task does not discharge.

[Persona]
Priya is brisk, mid-working-day, and businesslike. She volunteers only the surface request and her name
and mobile; date of birth, passport last four, the insurer's reference, the evidence reference and the
account of the incident come only when asked. Every fact she states points at a seeded row: the
approval letter is the decision of 2026-09-02, the fourteenth of August is the incident date on the
claim record, the seat home on the sixteenth is the 610.00 fare posted 2026-08-15 and the hotel to the
twenty-third is the reservation's check-out date. She is deliberately vague about money ('a few hundred
dollars, maybe more with the fee') so that no figure of gold can be parroted, and she does not know
whether the airline has paid her anything, which is exactly the fact the agent must establish from the
carrier's ledger rather than from her. Her passive reactions are bound to utterance events: she agrees
to the desk acting for her when asked; she runs the action handed to her once, when it is handed to
her; she closes when she is told the payment has been made. She never asks for a document, a statement
or anything else outside the gold.

[Standard solution]
Find the profile and verify. Read the policies, the premium lines, the whole claim record, the air
bookings and their ledger, and the hotel and its folio. From the claim record find the one approved
decision with no payment against it (travel delay, 750.00 allowed, incident 2026-08-14). Read the
payment rule and discover its two prerequisite sentences. From the carrier's ledger find the 120.00
paid on an involuntary schedule change and the 60.00 credit redeemed in full — compensation for a loss
the policy already settled (the missed connection payment of 250.00) — and book the recovery of 130.00.
Ask what else the cancellation cost her, establish that the journey was cut short on 16 August, compute
the amount claimed for the interruption head (1865.45 + 790.00 - 320.00 = 2335.45) and hand the filing
to her to lodge in her own name. Then pay the decided head: limit 1000.00, benefit consumed 520.00,
available 480.00, allowed 750.00, deductible 0.00, third-party offset 90.00, payment 390.00.

[Verification run]
Command: .venv/bin/python scratch/verify0.py (the handling-time evaluator built on
skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py; it replays the gold writes with the real tools
and evaluates each policy's compute on the world just before its own write).
  care_ext_third_party_recovery  result=130.0  history_rows=3  branches=16
    settlement_answered_rule 100.0 | money_counted_ground 220.0 | credit_valuation 70.0 |
    traveller_share_rule 180.0 | BASELINE(all)=100.0
  care_ext_claim_head_filing     result=2335.45 history_rows=4 branches=25
    journey_value_basis 2065.45 | unused_days_anchor 2542.73 | return_home_charges_counted 1545.45 |
    return_home_credit_offset 2395.45 | supplier_returned_rule 2655.45 | BASELINE(all)=1772.73
  care_ext_claim_payment_release result=390.0  history_rows=8  branches=18
    benefit_limit_by_head 660.0 | benefit_consumed_basis 260.0 | deductible_withheld_rule 340.0 |
    third_party_offset 480.0 | BASELINE(all)=700.0
  prerequisite sensitivity: payment without the recovery 260.0; payment without the filing 390.0 with
    the filed row absent from the terminal state.
  order swap (filing before recovery): payment 390.0 — identical, so the parallel edges leave the
    terminal state unambiguous.
These are exactly the values carried in computations and in the gold arguments.

[Two-way sweep rule <-> compute]
Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its rule sentence verbatim in
compute_basis — the four ladders of the payment, the four of the recovery and the five of the filing,
plus the aggregations behind them. Backward: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a
binding. The payment rule's sentences map to benefit_limit (the limit ladder), benefit_consumed (the
consumption ladder), deductible_withheld (the deductible ladder), settlement_offset (the third-party
ladder), benefit_available (never less than nothing), allowed_amount (the decision awaiting payment)
and result (the lower of, less the deductible), with the order and rounding sentence pinned on result.
The recovery rule's sentences map to settlement_answered, money_counted, credit_counted,
compensation_counted, traveller_share, compensation_available and result. The filing rule's sentences
map to journey_value, unused_days, journey_days, unused_value, return_home_charges, return_home_cost,
supplier_returned and result. Sensitive words checked: 'in the twelve months before the day the
recovery is booked' -> within_months=K('compensation_window_months'); 'raised on an airline
cancellation' -> reason_code filter; 'posted on or after the day the head decided arose' -> a DAYS
comparison; 'rounded to two decimal places' -> RND; 'never less than nothing' -> MX(...,0); 'the lower
of' -> MN.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context]
Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this worklog, and working only from the prose
that will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and the persona: the desk
finds one approved, unpaid decision; the payment rule's own prose says the payment waits on a recovery
standing on the record and on every benefit of the incident standing filed; the claim record shows no
recovery and one head for 14 August; the carrier's ledger shows compensation for the schedule change
and the fares and credit of the early return; the hotel's folio shows the refund. That reading gives
130.00, then 2335.45, then 390.00 — the same three numbers, in the same order, on the same three
objects. No second reading was found: the only candidate ambiguity, which payment the compensation
answers, is closed by the rule's own tier conditions, and the only candidate for 'the decision awaiting
payment' is the travel delay decision.

[Closure]
policy -> tool -> computation -> gold call -> terminal state:
care_ext_third_party_recovery -> book_benefit_recovery_c1be7196 -> computations[0] step 10 ->
  a care_claims recovery row of -130.00 restoring benefit;
care_ext_claim_head_filing -> file_benefit_claim_dde0dff5 (owner user) -> computations[1] step 12 ->
  a care_claims filed row claiming 2335.45;
care_ext_claim_payment_release -> release_claim_payment_9edda418 -> computations[2] step 14 ->
  a care_claims payment row of 390.00 with 0.00 withheld.
charter_scope claims exactly those three policies and three tools; required_documents repeats them in
order; no other policy or tool is touched, and no handoff is called.

[Manual values gates — task 0, run after the per-task scripts went green]
Length, breadth and the hidden test: walked from 'when do I get paid' to the payment through the two
prerequisite sentences of the payment rule; the parallel breadth at the payment is the head decided, the
ledger, the deductible ceiling and the carrier's ledger, and deleting any of the four moves the number
(660.00 / 260.00 / 340.00 / 480.00). One problem of the tree is the customer's own write and the filing
of a claim in one's own name is what the charter itself reserves to the policyholder; it completes on the
spot.
Need and simulator boundary: the customer states the object (the approved delay claim), the timing (now),
the authorisation (the desk may act, she files in her own name) and that a write is wanted. She never
reads policy, never corrects a figure and never names a prerequisite.
Opening chronology: every volunteered fact - the approval letter, the fourteenth of August, the seat home
on the sixteenth, the hotel paid to the twenty-third - points at a seeded row of the opening world; the
recovery, the second head and the payment are things only gold produces and she says nothing of them.
Base eligibility and the time anchor: care_claim_filing's deadline is the only time-shaped term on these
writes and it is checked by hand - incident 2026-08-14, plan deadline 30 days, frozen_time 2026-09-08 is
day 25, and 2026-09-14 would be the first day it failed. No eligibility of kind time applies to any of
the three subjects, so temporal_feasibility is [] rather than empty by oversight.
Authoritative facts and the business object: approval, payment and consumption all rest on care_claims
rows, never on the caller; the payment names the decision row it settles and the recovery the payment row
it reverses, so neither rests on the customer id alone.
Reachability and no real-world waits: the carrier paid on 2026-08-28 and the insurer decided on
2026-09-02, both before the call; the filing is the customer's own act performed while she is on the
line; nothing waits on a diagnosis, a clearing or a future date.
Prerequisite sentences: both pass the four-point test above, both are state-form and neither needed a
fallback, and each state is brought about by exactly one write of this difficulty.
rule/compute equivalence and honest labels: swept both ways; the two method factors change how a quantity
is computed (which payment a compensation answers, and whether consumption is recomputed from the ledger
or read from the record) rather than swapping a number in one formula, and the three parameter factors
select a limit, a deductible and an amount set against the settlement.
Draft recomputation from the visible context: recorded above; it reaches 130.00, 2335.45 and 390.00 with
no second reading found.

[Round 2 rework — items answered by id; no change to this task]

Item 1 was reported by the coordinator against "task 0's scored source_entry_id". This task's tools
take no source_entry_id: both derived writes carry `source_claim_id`, and each is uniquely entailed by
this task's own rules rather than left open. The recovery's is fixed by the tier that applied - "the
settlement the compensation answers is the payment made on the missed connection head" - and exactly
one payment on a missed connection head stands on the record. The payment's is fixed by "the figure
standing on the decision the insurer has allowed and that awaits payment", and exactly one approved
decision carries no payment against it. The runtime auditor reached both blind and matched them. The
defect is task 1's and is closed there; nothing in this task changed.

O1 (policy_kb 0.md note 1, runtime 0.md observation 3) — base care_subrogation's "the settlement is
reduced by what they received rather than recovered afterwards" against this task doing both. NOT
DECLARED, on the test of evaluating the same quantity once in the same world. Base states two rules,
not one: "Where a third party was liable for the loss the insurer may recover what it paid" governs a
settlement already made, and the reduce-rather-than-recover sentence governs a settlement now being
made. This task's two policies implement exactly that split - the payment being released is reduced by
the 90.00 the carrier paid for the same loss, and the recovery is booked only on a settlement paid on
2026-08-12, before any of the compensation feeding it existed. Declaring an overwrite here would retire
the very sentence the payment policy implements through its third-party offset, which would be wrong.

O2 (policy_kb 0.md note 2) — base care_claim_settlement's "cancellation and interruption are shares of
the declared trip cost" against the limit ladder's fall-through taking the whole declared trip cost.
NOT DECLARED: on this world the head decided is a travel delay, where both give the plan's travel delay
limit of 1000, so the quantities agree. Recorded for a future task that lets a cancellation or
interruption head await payment, which would make the two differ and require a declaration.

policy_kb 0.md note 3 — care_agg_benefit_coordination's "A recovery from a liable third party is
applied first to the policy that paid last" grounds no declared edge. NO CHANGE: it is a base sentence
about two policies answering one incident, and this world seeds one policy answering the incident and
one closed 2025 policy that answers nothing of it, so the clause is scoped out rather than contradicted.
No extended policy of this task states a cross-problem order beyond its own two prerequisite sentences.

policy_kb 0.md note 4 / runtime 0.md observation 2 — "every compensation" is plural while the machinery
resolves one settlement and one figure. NO CHANGE. The sentence is written at the strength the edge
intends: the payment waits until the record carries the recovery owed for each such compensation, and on
a record carrying one it is satisfied by one. Narrowing it to the singular would make the gate weaker
than the policy means and would have to be re-derived every time a second compensation appeared.

runtime 0.md observation 1 — she says she bought the seat home on the sixteenth while the ledger's
airline-cancellation fare posted on the fifteenth. NO CHANGE, and it is the designed boundary: the
factor counts from "the day that earlier return was bought" as the carrier's ledger carries it, and the
persona defers to the record in terms ("the desk should go by the record rather than her memory"). The
auditor resolved it to the fifteenth blind and matched gold.

runtime 0.md observation 4 — the travel delay daily ceiling of 250 is a base term the extended limit
ladder does not mention. NO CHANGE: it is unreached, not dropped. The binding quantity is the 480.00 of
benefit still available, and even read as a further cap on three days of delay it gives 750, above the
480.00 that binds. The insurer's allowance is the insurer's, which care_claim_assessment reserves to it.
user_scenario:
Priya Raghunathan is sixty-one, a structural engineer from the North Side of Chicago, and she is telephoning the travel protection desk on a Tuesday morning between site visits, so she is brisk and a little impatient but perfectly friendly. She says she is Priya Raghunathan, that the number the desk has for her is 7030114826, and that she is calling about the travel insurance she bought for her Portugal trip in August. Her opening is simple: the insurer wrote to her last week to say her claim for the delay on the way home had been approved, she has heard nothing since, and she would like the money paid out.

She is happy for the desk to act on her behalf on anything it can do itself, and says so plainly if asked - "you go ahead and do whatever needs doing at your end" - though she will not pretend to understand how the policy works and does not instruct the agent on what to do. If the desk needs her to confirm or lodge something in her own name, she will do it there and then while she is on the line, provided the agent explains in ordinary words what she is putting her name to and hands it over to her; she will not go looking for anything herself, and she will not act on anything the agent has not explained.

She gives her details only as they are asked for. Her date of birth is 1965-03-24. The last four characters of her passport are 3418. The reference the insurer quoted her for the trouble on the way home is WL-CLM-2026-31887, which she reads off the letter on her desk; she has no other reference numbers to hand and says so if pressed. She does not know her policy number or certificate number by heart and expects the desk to find them. If she is asked what the letter says was approved, she says only that it was approved and does not read out figures, because she says the letter is mostly small print and she would rather the desk look at the record than trust her reading of it.

Asked when the trouble happened, she says her flight home was cancelled on the fourteenth of August. Asked what that meant for the rest of the trip, she explains, without being asked twice, that she was stuck at Lisbon airport for the best part of three days, that in the end she gave up on the last week of the holiday and bought herself a seat home on the sixteenth, and that the hotel she had paid for up to the twenty-third went unused from that day. She is vague about money: she thinks the new ticket was "a few hundred dollars, maybe more with the fee", she cannot remember whether the airline sent her anything afterwards, and she says the desk should go by the record rather than her memory. If she is asked whether anyone else has paid her anything for the disruption, she says she is honestly not sure, there have been one or two emails from the airline, and she would rather the agent checked.

She travelled with her husband, who is named on the certificate with her, but the trouble and the costs were hers and any claim is in her own name as the first traveller on the certificate. The evidence she gave the insurer for the cancellation is the airline's disruption file TP-IRR-20260814, and she repeats that reference if she is asked what she sent in.

When the agent explains that something has to be put on her policy in her own name before matters can be settled, she does not argue and does not ask why; she says "fine, tell me what to press" and runs whatever the agent hands over to her, once, exactly as it is handed to her. When she is told a figure, she does not check it - she says she has no way of knowing whether it is right. If the agent tells her the payment has been made, she says that is all she wanted, thanks them for sorting it out and rings off. She never asks for anything to be sent to her, never raises a second matter, and if the agent goes quiet or asks her to wait she simply waits.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.care_policy_id: The policy the recovery is booked on. Basis: the profile lookup returns one travel protection policy standing expired on the 2026 Portugal journey, and the charter rule quoted verbatim is 'A recovery is applied against the payment it reverses and never against a different claim or a different policy.' Uniqueness: the traveller's other policy closed in 2025 with no claims on it, so only this policy carries a settled payment a recovery can attach to.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_claim_id: The payment row this recovery partly reverses. Basis: the extended rule states verbatim 'Where the carrier's ledger carries a payout raised on an involuntary schedule change and the claim record carries a payment made on a missed connection, the settlement the compensation answers is the payment made on the missed connection head'. Uniqueness: the claim record carries exactly one payment on a missed connection head, and the carrier's ledger carries a payout raised on an involuntary schedule change, so no other payment row answers the compensation.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_reference: The insurer's reference on the settlement being recovered against, copied from the claim record of that payment. Basis: the tool schema requires the reference 'copied character for character from the claim record'. Uniqueness: the payment row identified above carries this one reference and no other.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_type: The benefit the restored money was paid under. Basis: the same rule sentence fixes the settlement as 'the payment made on the missed connection head'. Uniqueness: the payment row's own head is a missed connection; every other head of the closed enum names a benefit no payment on that reference was made under, so none of them can describe the money being restored.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.recovered_amount_usd: The recovery computed at its own handling time. The settlement the compensation answers is the payment made on the missed connection head, 250.00; the money counted is what the carrier has paid on an involuntary schedule change in the twelve months before today, 120.00, the 260.00 paid on the closed 2024 booking falling outside that window; the travel credit counted is 60.00, the credit the carrier issued on that ground standing redeemed in full; the compensation counted is therefore 180.00; a deductible of 50.00 was withheld from that settlement and 180.00 is more than it, so 50.00 is set aside for the traveller and 130.00 is available to the insurer; the lower of 250.00 and 130.00 is 130.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the traveller's own filing action and hand it to her, since a claim is filed in the policyholder's own name.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock and call pair for a customer-owned write; it changes nothing in the record.

evaluation_criteria.objective: File the remaining head of the 14 August incident - the journey broken into - on the policy, in the traveller's own name and under the reference the insurer quoted.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The filing policy alone computes the amount claimed, and the payment on the decided head waits on every benefit that incident touched standing filed.

Basis: the tool schema requires 'the traveller reference number of the policyholder the claim belongs to'. Uniqueness: one profile answers the caller's name and mobile number.

Basis: the caller states verbatim 'The reference the insurer quoted her for the trouble on the way home is WL-CLM-2026-31887', and the extended rule states 'A claim is filed against one benefit under the reference the insurer quoted for the incident'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.paid_amount_usd: The payment computed at its own handling time, the world in which the recovery is booked and the second head stands filed. The head decided is a travel delay, so the benefit limit that applies is the plan's travel delay limit of 1000.00 rather than the declared trip cost; the claim record now carries a recovery, so the benefit consumed is the payments made, 650.00, less the recovery received, 130.00, which is 520.00, and not the 650.00 the policy record still shows; the benefit still available is therefore 480.00, which is lower than the 750.00 the insurer allowed; the deductibles already withheld on the policy come to 150.00 and the plan's ceiling on the total withheld is 150.00, so nothing remains of that ceiling and nothing is withheld; the carrier's ledger carries a payout of 90.00 raised on an airline cancellation posted on 2026-08-22, on or after the 14 August the head arose, so 90.00 is set against the settlement; 480.00 less 0.00 less 90.00 is 390.00.

Basis: the extended rule states verbatim 'where what remains of that ceiling is less than the plan's general deductible for each claim, the deductible withheld is only what remains of that ceiling'. Uniqueness: the three payments already made on this policy withheld 50.00 each, the plan's ceiling on the deductible withheld across one policy is 150.00, so nothing at all remains of it and no other figure can be withheld.

edges.condition: The policy's claim record carries a recovery row against every settlement for which a liable third party has paid the traveller compensation, so that the payments made less the recoveries received give the benefit the policy has truly consumed.
edges.policy_source: The money paid on a decided claim is worked out only after the policy's claim record carries the recovery owed for every compensation a liable third party has paid the traveller on a settlement already made under this policy.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the claim record carries no recovery at all: every row on the policy is a filing, a decision or a payment, while the carrier's ledger shows 120.00 paid on an involuntary schedule change on 2026-08-28 and a 60.00 credit issued on 2026-08-30 and redeemed on 2026-09-03 for the same disruption the missed connection head answered. The benefit the record shows consumed, 650.00, is therefore the whole of the payments made, with nothing restored.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Booking the recovery adds a care_claims row with event_type care_claim_recovery carrying -130.00 against the missed connection payment, so the payments made less the recoveries received become 520.00 and the benefit still available under the plan's travel delay limit rises from 350.00 to 480.00.

edges.condition: Every benefit the incident behind the decided claim has touched stands on the policy's claim record as a claim filed under the reference the insurer quoted for that incident.
edges.policy_source: A payment is released on a decided claim only once every benefit the same incident has touched stands filed on the policy, because one incident is settled as one case.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 14 August incident carries one head only on the claim record, the travel delay filed on 2026-08-19 and decided on 2026-09-02. The same incident also cut the journey short - the seat home was bought on 2026-08-15 and the guest left the Lisbon property on 2026-08-16 against a reservation booked to 2026-08-23 - and no head for that loss stands filed on the policy under the insurer's reference or any other.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Filing the interruption head adds a care_claims row with event_type care_claim_file and claim_status filed under WL-CLM-2026-31887, so both benefits the incident touched stand filed and the case is complete.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and may be written in either order. The verification run replayed both orders on the same seed: with the recovery first the payment is 390.00, with the filing first the payment is 390.00, and the terminal rows are identical because the two writes touch disjoint objects - the recovery row is keyed on the missed connection payment and carries event_type care_claim_recovery, the filed row is keyed on the new reference and head and carries claim_status filed with paid_amount_usd 0.00, so neither enters the other's aggregates (the payment's consumption reads payout and recovery rows only, and the filing reads decision rows only).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the recovery and replaying everything else leaves the benefit consumed at 650.00 instead of 520.00, so the benefit still available falls from 480.00 to 350.00 and the scored payment falls from 390.00 to 260.00.

Skipping the filing leaves the terminal state without the care_claims row claiming 2335.45 on the interruption head, so the terminal hash differs from gold; the payment itself stays at 390.00, which is why this edge is declared state_gate rather than value_input.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions a recovery, compensation received from the carrier, a second claim, a head not yet filed, or anything that must be settled first, and it contains no phrase of the 'do I need to sort something out first' kind.
